title: Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
sourceText:
Biological Sciences [BSCI] with lab
To meet College of Arts and Sciences requirements, students must complete 1 additional lab credit of [BSCI] or [PSCI] for a total of 8 credits (2 labs).

ENGLISH 101 [WRTG]

Social Sciences [SSCI]

WGSS 101 [DIVR] or WGSS 120 [DIVR]

HISTORY 105 [ROOT]

Physical Sciences [PSCI] with lab
To meet College of Arts and Sciences requirements, students must complete 1 additional lab credit of [BSCI] or [PSCI] for a total of 8 credits (2 labs).

Quantitative Reasoning [QUAN]

WGSS Field Elective
WGSS Field Electives (12 credits): Approved courses include WGSS 101, 120, 220, 301 , 321, 338, 340, 406, 410, 460, 477, 485 [M], 499; CRM J/WGSS 403; ENGLISH/WGSS 309, 317; WGSS 332/ANTH 317; WGSS/ENGLISH 211; WGSS/ENGLISH/SOC 300 [M]; WGSS/HISTORY 336, 369; WGSS/SOC 302.
Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Field and Interdisciplinary Electives (21 credits): 12 credits of Field Electives and 9 credits of Interdisciplinary Electives required. 15 of the 21 credits must be at the 300-400 level and to meet University requirements electives must include one [M] course. Courses may not be used to fulfill more than one requirement.

Electives
Electives: Students are encouraged to pursue an additional major, minor, or certificate. Electives should include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirements of 40 upper-division credits.

Arts [ARTS]

Communication [COMM] or Written Communication [WRTG]

Foreign Language, if needed, or Electives
Electives: Students are encouraged to pursue an additional major, minor, or certificate. Electives should include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirements of 40 upper-division credits.
Two years of high school foreign language or at least two semesters of college-level foreign language are required by the College of Arts and Sciences for graduation.

Humanities [HUM]

Equity and Justice [EQJS]

Foreign Language, if needed,  or Electives
Electives: Students are encouraged to pursue an additional major, minor, or certificate. Electives should include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirements of 40 upper-division credits.
Two years of high school foreign language or at least two semesters of college-level foreign language are required by the College of Arts and Sciences for graduation.

WGSS 406, WGSS 332/ANTH 317, or WGSS 340

Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Interdisciplinary Elective
Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Interdisciplinary Electives (9 Credits): Approved courses include AMDT/WGSS 422; AMER ST/DTC/ENGLISH 475; AMER ST/ENGLISH/HISTORY/WGSS 216; ANTH/WGSS 316; BIOLOGY 307; CES 435, 454; CES/ANTH 312; CES/WGSS 411; COM/WGSS 464; ENGLISH/WGSS 306 [M]; ENGLISH 483/WGSS 382; ART/WGSS 308 [M], 310 [M]; HISTORY/CES 235; HISTORY/WGSS 398, 399; MUS/WGSS 363; PHIL/WGSS 425; POL S 305/WGSS 305; PSYCH/WGSS 230, 324; SOC/WGSS 251, 351, 384, 390; WGSS/PHIL 462 [M].
Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Field and Interdisciplinary Electives (21 credits): 12 credits of Field Electives and 9 credits of Interdisciplinary Electives required. 15 of the 21 credits must be at the 300-400 level and to meet University requirements electives must include one [M] course. Courses may not be used to fulfill more than one requirement.

Complete Writing Portfolio

WGSS/SOC 385

WGSS 481 [M]

WGSS 403 [CAPS] or 495 [CAPS]

300-400-level Electives
Electives: Students are encouraged to pursue an additional major, minor, or certificate. Electives should include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirements of 40 upper-division credits.

This program is not accepting majors at this time.  For more information about undergraduate courses, minors, or certificate options, please contact Professor Melissa Nicolas (melissa.nicolas@wsu.edu)

A student may be admitted to the Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies major upon making their intention known to the program. The major in Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies requires a minimum of 36 credits, of which 15 credits are required in the major, 12 credits are required in Field Electives, and 9 credits are required in Interdisciplinary Electives. 15 credits of electives must be at the 300-400 level.
